content.text: {"quote_faithful": "yes", "verdict": "confirmed", "evidence_kind": "missing_justification", "fatal": "no", "explanation": "Section 3 proves only that V contains at most one positive value, so the exhaustive case list is V={0}, V={c}, V={0,c}. The text lists only (i) g\u22610 and (ii) 'V \u2286 {0,c} with both values attainable', so the pure case V={c} (g\u2261c>0, 0 not attained) is indeed absent from the enumeration; the objection reads the quote correctly. However, this omitted case needs no argument at all: V={c} means g(x)=c for every x, i.e. f(x)=x+c, which is the desired conclusion, and \u00a77 states exactly this ('the function g never takes the value 0. Together with \u00a73 this forces g(x) \u2261 c'). So the defect is one of exposition/logical bookkeeping, not of mathematical content; the necessity argument as written still yields f(x)=x+c in every case."}
